line: Welcome. I'm Guo, I chair the association. You found us without anyone dragging you here. For your generation, that's already unusual.
choice1: My mom told me about this place.

line: Then she raised you well. We run the Saturday school, the festival, the seniors' lunch. Everything here, we built ourselves. No grants, no strings.
The Mid-Autumn committee needs people who can lift tables and also read a spreadsheet. It's a rare combination.
You have a good head. I wish you were here more. The city says partner, partner. When the money stops, who is still here? Us.
The festival committee has dinner at my house Sunday. Only the core people. I want you there. My wife is making red-braised pork, so skip lunch.
You see now why we keep a lawyer's number on our board. Washington changes its mind every four years. The association is still here.
Everyone is excited about the new president. Fine. In four years, someone else. The Saturday school has been here forty-one years.
choice1: Forty-one years is a long time.

line: Ah, the library regular. Dr. Zhou tells me you go to Ruth Hale's potlucks. I hope they feed you well.
choice2: I still come here, Mr. Guo.

line: You're here so often I keep forgetting you're not on the committee. We should fix that.
